paragraphs.title: God’s Presence and Victory over Weapons of War

easy.explanation: The verse says, “In Judah is God known.”
easy.q: Where is God known according to verse 1?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 says, “In Salem also is his tabernacle.”
easy.q: Where is God’s tabernacle said to be?

answers: The arrows, shield, sword, and battle
easy.explanation: Verse 3 says that God broke the arrows of the bow, the shield, the sword, and the battle.

medium.explanation: The first verse declares, “his name is great in Israel.”
medium.q: What is said about God’s name in Israel?

medium.explanation: A dwelling place is a place where someone lives or resides.
medium.q: What does the word “dwelling” mean in the phrase “his dwelling place in Zion”?

medium.explanation: Verse 2 says, “his dwelling place in Zion.”
medium.q: Which location is paired with Salem as God’s dwelling place?

answers: God is known in Judah, dwells in Salem and Zion, and breaks weapons of war
God hides from Israel, gathers an army, and builds a city
God judges the meek, receives gifts, and terrifies kings
challenge.explanation: The verses move from God’s reputation to His dwelling and then to His victory over weapons.
challenge.q: What sequence of ideas appears in verses 1–3?

answers: God’s presence is associated with victory over human warfare
Zion is portrayed as an enemy of God
The weapons are used to build God’s dwelling
challenge.explanation: The passage places God’s dwelling in Salem and Zion and then describes His defeat of the weapons of war.
challenge.q: What does the connection between Salem, Zion, and the broken weapons suggest?

challenge.explanation: The phrase appears with the shield, sword, and battle, so it refers to weapons of war.
challenge.q: What is the likely meaning of “the arrows of the bow” in verse 3?

paragraphs.title: The Enemies Submit to God’s Power

answers: They are spoiled and sleep their sleep
easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “The stouthearted are spoiled, they have slept their sleep.”
Verse 5 says that none of the men of might found their hands.
easy.q: Who could not find their hands?

answers: They were cast into a dead sleep
easy.explanation: Verse 6 says that the chariot and horse were cast into a dead sleep at God’s rebuke.
easy.q: What happened to the chariot and horse?

medium.explanation: The stouthearted are those who are strong or bold in courage.
medium.q: What does “stouthearted” most nearly mean in this passage?

medium.explanation: Verse 6 directly connects their helplessness with God’s rebuke.
medium.q: What caused the chariot and horse to become powerless?

medium.explanation: In context, the men of might were so defeated that they could not use their strength.
medium.q: What does the expression “found their hands” imply?

answers: All are rendered powerless before God
challenge.explanation: The passage describes both warriors and military equipment as helpless before God.
challenge.q: What do the stouthearted, men of might, chariot, and horse have in common?

answers: God’s overwhelming power contrasts with the weakness of the enemy
The quiet earth contrasts with the noisy city
The gifts of the people contrast with the anger of man
challenge.explanation: God’s power is emphasized while the enemy’s strength collapses.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in verses 5–7?

answers: God defeats both the soldiers and the means by which they fight
The army escapes while the chariot remains
challenge.explanation: The passage broadens the defeat from human fighters to the chariot and horse that support warfare.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from mentioning both warriors and military animals?

paragraphs.title: Divine Judgment Brings Fear and Stillness

easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, “Thou didst cause judgment to be heard from heaven.”
easy.q: What did God cause to be heard from heaven?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the earth feared, and was still.”

answers: All the meek of the earth
easy.explanation: Verse 9 says that God arose to save all the meek of the earth.
easy.q: Whom did God save when He arose to judgment?

answers: The gifts brought by the people
medium.explanation: The earth’s fear follows the judgment that God caused to be heard from heaven.
medium.q: What caused the earth to fear?

medium.explanation: The meek are humble, gentle, and not self-exalting.
medium.q: What does “meek” mean in the phrase “the meek of the earth”?

medium.explanation: Verse 9 specifically says that He arises to save all the meek of the earth.
medium.q: What happens when God arises to judgment?

answers: Judgment is heard from heaven, the earth fears and becomes still, and God saves the meek
The earth rejoices, the kings bring presents, and the warriors triumph
The chariot advances, the horse awakens, and the meek flee
challenge.explanation: This follows the progression of the two verses.

answers: God’s judgment causes the earth to fear and become quiet
The earth becomes quiet before judgment is announced
Stillness causes the earth to reject God’s judgment
challenge.explanation: The verse presents fear and stillness as responses to God’s heavenly judgment.
challenge.q: How are fear and stillness related in the passage?

answers: God’s judgment defeats opposition while saving the humble
God saves the mighty and condemns the humble
The passage treats both groups exactly alike
challenge.explanation: The judgment setting includes both divine authority over opposition and salvation for the meek.
challenge.q: What distinction does the passage make between the wicked and the meek?

paragraphs.title: Response to Salvation and Recognition of God’s Sovereignty

answers: Vow and pay unto the LORD
easy.explanation: Verse 11 says, “Vow, and pay unto the LORD your God.”
easy.q: What should people do with their vows?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “let all that be round about him bring presents unto him.”
easy.q: What should those round about God bring unto Him?

easy.explanation: Verse 12 says, “he is terrible to the kings of the earth.”

answers: He restrains the remainder of it
He allows it to overcome Him
He hides it from the kings
medium.explanation: Verse 10 says, “the remainder of wrath shalt thou restrain.”
medium.q: What does God do with the wrath of man?

medium.explanation: The people are called to bring gifts or offerings to God.
medium.q: What does “presents” mean in this context?

answers: As a response of worship and acknowledgment of God
To make the kings less fearful
medium.explanation: These actions express gratitude, worship, and recognition of God’s authority.
medium.q: Why are people called to vow, pay, and bring presents?

answers: God can use, limit, and restrain human wrath
Human wrath is stronger than God’s power
God has no authority over human anger
challenge.explanation: The verse presents even the remainder of human wrath as subject to God’s restraint.
challenge.q: What relationship between human wrath and God’s rule is shown in verse 10?

answers: God restrains wrath, people fulfill vows and bring gifts, and God cuts off the spirit of princes
The earth trembles, the chariot awakens, and the meek bring weapons
The kings make vows, God hides His presence, and Judah falls
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from God’s control of wrath to human worship and finally to His judgment on rulers.

answers: God’s authority reaches both worshipers and earthly rulers
Only ordinary people must honor God
The kings are exempt from God’s judgment
challenge.explanation: The passage calls those around God to bring presents and declares that He is terrible even to kings.
challenge.q: What is suggested by the movement from those around God to the kings of the earth?
